findings: NUMBERING ZONE FOUND FROM BYTES: MT 21:1-5 = WEB 20:45-49; MT 21:6-37 = WEB 21:1-32; identity elsewhere. Totals equal at 1273, so it is a shift, not a gap. Confirmed by CONTENT (MT 21:1 is the word-event formula that WEB prints at 20:45), not by arithmetic alone, because equal totals would also fit a gap plus a surplus. The Tier-0 dual-reference rule now binds any ref touching WEB 20:45-49, WEB ch 21 or MT ch 21. This is NOT Jeremiah's zone (MT 8:23 = WEB 9:1) and was not assumed from it.

SELF-CAUGHT EXTRACTION DEFECT (1): the first OSHB extractor leaked the tail of the <verse> open tag, so every MT verse began with a stray '>'. Caught by reading the extracted text back, not by the regex looking right.

SELF-CAUGHT EXTRACTION DEFECT (2): the first extractor stripped seg TAGS but kept their CONTENT, injecting maqaf, paseq and sof-pasuq into the running MT text. The established convention, derived by reading Lam.xml against the shipped Lam extract rather than assumed, is that every seg is dropped WITH its content and the morpheme separator '/' removed. Now asserted: 0 occurrences of U+05BE, U+05C0, U+05C3, '/' and '>'.

SELF-CAUGHT INVENTORY DEFECT (3): the mark inventory required a type= attribute on <note> and silently dropped every untyped note. It surfaced only because the sof-pasuq count (1272) did not close against 1273 verses. Fixing it recovered 71 verses of OSHB editorial notes - ketiv/qere divergences from BHS and consonant/vowel/accent readings - i.e. 71 textual-variant disclosure sites that would otherwise have been invisible to every downstream lane.

ARITHMETIC ANOMALIES CHASED AND RESOLVED: Ezek 33:20 carries no sof-pasuq, standing instead with an untyped OSHB note ('We read punctuation in L differently from BHS') followed by a pe mark - a real single-witness divergence, not a parsing gap. Ezek 43:27 carries two consecutive samekh segs, so 184 mark occurrences stand on 183 verses; occurrences and verses are reported separately and never added.

SELF-CAUGHT INVENTORY DEFECT (4): the hand-of-YHWH pattern fixed the word order and returned 1 in a book where the motif stands in 7 verses; and the dateline pattern first lumped 3 festival-calendar dates in ch 45 with the oracle datelines, then, matching only the construct form, returned ZERO datelines in a book famous for them. Both counts were disbelieved on their face and corrected: 7 hand-of-YHWH verses, 13 oracle datelines, 3 calendar dates kept separate because they open no oracle.

CORROBORATION: 'son of man' stands in 93 verses, the standard count for Ezekiel, and the 13 datelines are the standard set (1:1, 1:2, 8:1, 20:1, 26:1, 29:1, 29:17, 30:20, 31:1, 32:1, 32:17, 33:21, 40:1). This corroborates the extraction; it is not a segmentation input.
LANGUAGE LAYER: morph prefixes are H only across 18,866 tokens - no Aramaic island, unlike Jeremiah MT 10:11.

SPECIAL-MARK CLASS FOUND THAT THE SEG SWEEP MISSED: puncta extraordinaria at MT 41:20 and MT 46:22. The seg-type sweep returned zero for x-large, x-small, reversed nun and suspended letter, and it would have been easy to publish 'Ezekiel has no special scribal marks'. The note layer says otherwise. SEAM SIGNIFICANCE OF THE NUMBERING ZONE: a PE (petuchah) stands at MT 21:5 = WEB 20:49, so the Masoretic tradition closes a unit exactly at the English chapter break. The zone is a seam site as well as a numbering site, which is why it is on the flagged list.
